conviction_note: The Q3 print will probably beat. ASE's ATM business grew +20% QoQ against its own +11-13% guide, and Amkor beat the top of its Q2 range by $50M with $0.70 EPS against a $0.52 top. This name trades on the guide, though: it fell 24.7% on a large Q2 beat because the guide was soft. The Q4 guide faces October news on both sides. Against it: iPhone 18 Pro orders cut by at least 15%, global smartphone units down 20-22% on memory costs, and the SiP move to Vietnam running into Q4. For it: the Nvidia Vera/HDFO volume ramp in Q4. All of this lands on a stock already down 28.5% in 20 days, with puts bid (skew +17.6). The findings net to about +0.1. p_up is 49 (scale 12), so the scaled number is -0.24. The two measurements agree that there is no usable direction. The likely Q3 beat (print_vs_bar +1.7%) has repeatedly not paid on this name.
bar: Q3 2026 net sales consensus $2.02-2.03B and EPS $0.77-0.79. Two sources roughly agree: Investing.com 2026-10-26 ($2.03B / $0.774, https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/amkor-earnings-on-deck-as-ai-packaging-bets-face-stock-slump-test-93CH-4931974) and Zacks via Yahoo 2026-10-21 ($2.02B / $0.79, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-projections-key-metrics-reveal-184212797.html). Company guide is $1.95-2.05B, GM 18.5-19.5%, EPS $0.72-0.82 (8-K 2026-07-27, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001047127/000104712726000043/amkr6302026erex-991.htm). Consensus sits slightly above the guide midpoint. Zacks expects communications at 36.0% of mix (51.0% a year ago) and computing at 24.4%. Q4 2026 bar: no direct multi-analyst source. It is DERIVED from the Zacks FY2026 consensus of $7.64B revenue and $2.60 EPS less Q1-Q3, giving Q4 of about $2.04B and about $0.79 EPS, roughly flat on Q3 (MarketBeat shows one Q4 estimate of $0.52). Findings that depend on the Q4 bar are capped small for that reason. On the July call management said there would be 'no significant second-half lift, even into Q4' and that GM would be about flat if mix and utilisation hold (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/AMKR/Q22026).

findings.finding: Peer ASE (the largest OSAT) reported Q3 2026 ATM (assembly, test, materials) revenue of NT$151.5B on 2026-10-12. That is +20.1% QoQ in NT$ (+18.7% in US$) and +51% YoY. ASE had guided Q3 ATM to +11-13% QoQ in late July, so it beat its own guide by about 7-9 points. Amkor's Q3 guide midpoint ($2.0B) implies only about +5% QoQ from $1.898B. This supports Amkor printing at or above the top of its $1.95-2.05B range against a $2.02-2.03B consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $1.90B against a $1.75-1.85B guide and EPS $0.70 against a $0.52 top, yet the stock fell 24.74% on the Q3 guide. Q3 2025 beat and the stock fell 3.07%. On this name a reported-quarter beat has been sold or ignored when the guide disappoints.
findings.why_not_priced: It was public from 2026-10-12, yet AMKR fell about 20% after it while ASE's data pointed up. Consensus EPS and revenue for AMKR were unchanged over 30 days (Zacks), so nobody carried the peer beat into Amkor's Q3 number. Had they, the Q3 revenue consensus would sit above the $2.05B top of the guide rather than at $2.02-2.03B. This is a proxy: ASE's growth is weighted to leading-edge/AI packaging in Taiwan, while Amkor's Q3 has a communications drag that ASE does not share to the same degree.
findings.independence: ASE's own Q2 call guidance of +11-13% (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/ase-technology-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-30/) is the comparison. TSMC's Q3 revenue was +50.9% YoY with CoWoS demand cited (https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3346, 2026-10-15). Both are peers or proxies, not Amkor's own number.

findings.finding: Amkor's own recent pattern is to print above the top of its revenue guide. Q2 2026 revenue was $1.898B against a guide of $1.75-1.85B, and EPS was $0.70 against $0.42-0.52. Q2 was up 13% QoQ, and the Q3 guide asks only about +5% with computing guided up nearly 30% sequentially.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As above, the Q2 2026 beat was followed by -24.74%. Beats are not paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS ($0.77-0.79) sits near the Q3 guide midpoint ($0.77), not near the top, even though the last quarter landed $0.18 above the top of the range. If the pattern were priced, the Q3 EPS consensus would be about $0.85 or higher.
findings.independence: Company documents only. It shares the Q3 beat thesis with the ASE finding but rests on a different source.

findings.finding: Global smartphone shipments fell 20% YoY in Q3 2026 (Counterpoint) or 22% to 255.3M units (IDC preliminary), the weakest Q3 since 2012, driven by DRAM/NAND costs. IDC sees 2026 down 16.7%, and Counterpoint sees no volume recovery until component costs ease (possibly late 2027). Amkor's communications segment was 42% of Q2 sales. Amkor guided Q3 communications down high single digits QoQ and said Android revenue fell 20% QoQ in Q2 on memory. Apple, Amkor's largest communications customer, gained share from 18% to 22%, so Apple units were roughly flat YoY. The read is worse for Android than for Amkor's Apple-heavy mix. For the Q4 guide, the memory squeeze has no visible end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: guided communications down high single digits and Q3 revenue about 5% below consensus, and the stock fell 24.74%. The communications line moves this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Zacks consensus already models communications at 36% of Q3 sales against 51% a year earlier, which implies communications revenue down about 28% YoY, and the stock fell about 28% after these data. The open question is the Q4 communications guide, where the derived consensus has total Q4 flat on Q3.
findings.independence: Counterpoint (https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/news/story/global-smartphone-shipments-hit-a-14-year-low-in-q3-amid-a-memory-shortage-561272-2026-10-13) and IDC agree. Amkor's own July call cited memory constraints. It shares the memory-cost cause with the iPhone finding below but is a different data set (global units against Apple Pro orders).

findings.finding: Nikkei Asia (via Reuters, 2026-10-09) reported that Apple cut iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max component orders for October by at least 15% against original requests, on soft demand after a $100 price rise tied to memory costs. Amkor said in July that one SiP application's Korea-to-Vietnam transfer extends into Q4 and H1 2027, and that there would be 'no significant second-half lift, even into Q4'. The derived Q4 consensus (about $2.04B, roughly flat QoQ) leaves room for a Q4 guide below it if Apple communications volume falls. Q4 2025 was itself -5% QoQ.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (July): a Q3 revenue guide about 5% under consensus, driven by communications, took the stock down 24.74%. Feb 2026: Q4 2025 was -5% QoQ and the Q1 guide drew +1.79%. Q3 2025 print: -3.07%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is -28.5% over 20 days with skew at +17.6. But consensus was unchanged over 30 days (Zacks), and the FY2026 consensus of $7.64B still implies Q4 flat on Q3. If the cut were in estimates, Q4 revenue would be modelled down QoQ and FY revenue would be under $7.6B. Caveats: Reuters could not verify the report, component orders are not output, and computing growth offsets part of it (next finding). The Q4 bar is derived from one FY consensus, so this is capped.
findings.independence: B. Riley cut its target to $46 from $65 on 2026-10-20 citing communications-segment risk (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/nebenwerte/amkor-technology-stock-falls-3-88-percent-b-riley-cuts-target-to-usd-46-00/70378371). The July call transcript covers the SiP transfer into Q4 (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/AMKR/Q22026). It shares the memory-cost driver with the smartphone finding.

findings.finding: Computing (22% of Q2 sales, guided up nearly 30% QoQ in Q3) has a Q4 volume driver. Nvidia said Vera Rubin ships initially in Q3 with a larger volume ramp in Q4 2026. UBS tied Amkor's HDFO CPU ramp to Nvidia's Vera CPU when upgrading to Buy with a $90 target in July. Management said the CPU program 'began ramping in Q2 and is expected to keep scaling through H2', with four 2.5D and four HDFO product launches in 2026. This partly offsets communications in the Q4 guide: at about 24-27% of sales, a +15-20% QoQ computing step adds roughly $80-100M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: the Nvidia $1.5B partnership headline drew +17% after hours and the UBS upgrade +7% (late July). AI/computing news has moved this stock up when it is the headline. At the Q2 print it was outweighed by the communications guide.
findings.source_date: 2026-05 (Nvidia Q1 FY2027 call summary); UBS note 2026-07-24
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus Q4 is flat on Q3 (derived), which is consistent with management's 'no H2 lift' and gives no visible credit for a Q4 Vera volume step. The stock's -28% October slide was driven by smartphone/memory and semicap news, not by any AI-demand cut. A proxy: Amkor has not quantified Vera content, and the Q4 bar is derived, so the size is capped.
findings.independence: UBS upgrade note (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/this-nvda-partners-stock-jumps-7-percent-why-ubs-sees-38-percent-upside-for-amkor-technology/cZZp2YcR7zI). TSMC Q3 strength and CoWoS demand (https://pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3346). The ASE Q3 beat is evidence of strong AI packaging demand industry-wide (shares the ASE source with finding 1 for the industry read only).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 AMKR fell 10.1-10.7% in a sector selloff triggered by Lam Research's call warning that equipment parts and cleanroom bottlenecks limit tool supply through 2027 (Nasdaq -2.6% that day). There was no Amkor-specific news. For Amkor the read is mixed: it may slow advanced-packaging capacity adds, and it may hold 2026 capex ($2.5-3.0B) toward the low end, which helps free cash flow. Part of the pre-print drawdown is sector beta that the print can unwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of a sector-driven pre-print drawdown in the baseline. In July the stock fell 24.7% on company-specific guidance, not sector beta.
findings.why_not_priced: Weak. It rests on inference that a sector-driven fall overshoots for a packaging house. If the market had separated the Lam news from Amkor fundamentals, AMKR would have recovered on 10-23 to 10-26. Instead it is lower ($38.0 at the 17:11 UTC seal against $39.30 on 10-23).
findings.independence: Tickeron 2026-10-22 lists sector weakness among the causes of the slide (https://tickeron.com/blogs/amkor-technology-amkr-stock-falls-27-6-in-30-days-key-factors-and-outlook-20708/).

The stock is -28.5% over 20 days, ran 10 straight down sessions to 2026-10-16 (-25.3%, Trefis), and is -59% from its 52-week high of $96.68. 25d skew is +17.6 with early-October put/call volume about 2.38. Mean target is about $74.50 with 11 Buys, against a $38 spot. Short interest is moderate (about 8.9% of float, about 2.6 days to cover, Fintel undated). findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q2 -24.7% the stock did not reprice back up. Up on only 2 of the last 7 prints (+1.79%, +18.13%). The +18.13% (July 2025) came after a period of depressed expectations.
findings.why_not_priced: This IS the price, so it is the thing being bet against, not an unpriced fact. The skew says downside is paid for. The sign runs against the skew because the known negatives (smartphone collapse, iPhone Pro cuts, B. Riley's cut) have been public for 1-3 weeks and absorbed in a 28% fall. The option market prices the size of the guide risk, not its sign. Sized small because the skew has won such cases before.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline's options block (skew +17.6, implied 11.76%) and Tickeron 2026-10-22 on the put/call ratio.

findings.finding: 2026 capex guide of $2.5-3.0B (65-70% facilities including Arizona phase one) and long-term debt up to $2.33B from $1.28B in H1. Management flagged US manufacturing burden as a 2027 headwind and Arizona ramp dilution in 2028. Asked what the money buys: TSMC's 10-year procurement agreement, a multi-year Nvidia partnership with a 2027 prepayment, and an Arizona phase one described as 'fully committed'. The spend is corroborated, so the financing is not distress. A first 2027 capex or margin framing on this call is a modest risk to the multiple.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: capex at $2.5-3.0B was a secondary cause of the -24.7% (Motley Fool, Insider Monkey).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. These headwinds were disclosed in July and sit inside what the company already told the market. Only an incremental 2027 capex number would be new.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K balance sheet and cash flow (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001047127/000104712726000043/amkr6302026erex-991.htm). baseline_tension: Mixed. The negative guidance findings agree with the skew and the run-up and are largely priced. The Q3 beat and computing findings cut against the skew, and the reaction history (beats sold, 5 of 7 prints down) says the beat will not carry the stock. That leaves p_up just under 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells its beats): ASE Q3-beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6 and own-beat-pattern finding from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 3 (own caveat must reach the number): smartphone-collapse finding cut from -1.0 to -0.5, because consensus already models communications -28% YoY and Apple gained share.
Lesson 6 (bar unsourced or derived): Q4 consensus is derived from one FY figure, so the Q4-guide findings were capped. iPhone cut went from -2.0 to -1.5 and computing/Vera from +1.0 to +0.8.
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0; inference loses to documents): Lam/sector-beta positioning finding cut from +0.5 to +0.2.
Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew needs a reason or a smaller size): reset-bar positioning finding cut from +1.0 to +0.5, with the reason stated in why_not_priced.

Lesson 4 / 6 (financing is a question; inside what the company already guided): capex/financing finding moved from -0.3 to -0.1, because the spend is corroborated by the TSMC and Nvidia agreements and the headwinds were disclosed in July.
Scaled measurement: p_up moved from 48 to 49 (several lessons push toward 50). abs_move_pct stays at 12.0, near the 11.76% implied move. Sum moved from +0.4 to +0.1.
